headNote: `head` names the commit this pass ran at, cited as its replay in this history - this branch's twenty-one commits replayed onto `c0570ea60` (`main`, 0.19.7: the 0.19.7 bump, #118's one-frame submit/echo seam, #136's clear control in the sidebar search field, #137's packaging split and #138's per-arch macOS artifacts and delta-capable updates). `head` cannot cite the commit it rides in with: a commit cannot name its own sha. `main` has since moved three more times - `6f9bc2d04` (#140, the desktop toolchain: Electron 44 and TypeScript 7), `4ffc3f2b5` (#139, the New chat row aligned with All chats) and `ad09ec6b4` (the 0.20.1 release) - and this branch was MERGED UP onto that rather than replayed onto it, so `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` below are the MERGED head's trees, the pair `check-evidence.mjs` asserts against `HEAD:src`/`HEAD:scripts` at the docs commit that carries these frames, while `head` names the pre-#139/#140 commit the pass itself ran at. They are two different trees by design, and a reader reconciling the stamps should read them that way; `provenanceNote` says exactly which surfaces that gap touches and which it does not, and the short version is that neither upstream change is in the import closure of any frame this branch contributed. The rest of this manifest is the merged tree, counted off it rather than added from either side: this branch's mentioned-files sets, and `main`'s own evidence since the branch's base (the model-picker set and its `previousRefresh` record, the `chat-tool-rows` 4px-rejected comparison, `clear-search`, `new-chat-row`, and the swept frames). `dirtyWorkingTree` is true and that is not code: the untracked design note `docs/mentioned-files-design.md` sits in the tree and the capture's dirtiness test excludes only `docs/evidence`, so the two tree hashes still name source rather than a work in progress.

countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 882 at this commit, re-derived from the TREE rather than carried forward: 1054 `.webp` are committed and the 22 declared sets below account for 172 of them. Both terms move with the branch's rebases, and never in the branch's own direction alone: `main`'s merges arrive with new frames AND new declarations (`clear-search`, `new-chat-row`, `mentioned-files-app`, plus six earlier), and a merge that kept only one side of the declared list would silently move whole sets in or out of this count. The conflict in this file is therefore resolved as the UNION of both lists and the count re-derived from the tree afterwards. This branch's own set is unchanged in size (39 run-panel stories, 78 frames) — re-taken this round, which changes bytes, not counts. `check-evidence.mjs` fails when the number and the tree disagree.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 144, of which 39 are this PR's run-panel surfaces. `main`'s later merges added the rest (the model-picker and canvas surfaces, the clear-search set, `#128`'s mentioned-files stories); this branch adds the two newest (`roster-members` for the membership rule, `reader-child-controls` for the descend control's singular label). `check-evidence.mjs` counts the list and fails a mismatch, so this field cannot lag its source.
countsMean.themes: `THEMES.length` - the twelve brand palettes; the live pair is the two brand themes only, because it proves behaviour rather than colour.

partialCapture.note: This set is not a full sweep and does not claim to be. Ten stories were re-taken in the two brand themes through the rig at :6055, one `--only=` run per story, with a backend permitted on the configured port (no captured surface talks to it): the two new frames and the eight whose rendering this round's fixes move. SIX of those ten came back with different bytes - twelve frames: `todos-implicit-phase` (the unnamed group's boundary), `reader-pending` and `reader-gone` (the two absence lines), `mcp-auth-required` and `mcp-unknown-status` (the tally's singular) and `mcp-disconnected` (the canonical projection's failure text on a problem row). The two new stories add four more (`roster-members`, `reader-child-controls`), so this pass wrote 22 frames in total and sixteen frames are new or changed on disk. `reader-live` was re-taken and came back byte-identical, which is stated in the README rather than claimed as a change: a still cannot carry a ticking number, and that is the one claim in this round whose evidence is a measurement rather than a picture. Every other frame in the set is untouched by this pass, and the rest of the sweep describes surfaces this change does not touch. `dirtyWorkingTree: true` is the record that the capture ran against the working tree rather than against a commit. Round 2 re-took the whole set — all thirty-nine run-panel stories in both themes, one `--only=` run per story through the rig at :6055 — for two separate reasons: this branch's MCP row now renders the remedy AND the diagnosis (§ 7.2, U2-2), which moves the MCP problem-row frames, and `main`'s `#128` moved the header this column mounts, which moves the column of every frame that has one. The three to-do frames came back byte-identical (the U2-3 clamp only paints differently for a reason too long for its line, and the fixtures' reasons fit); the rest differ by the anti-aliasing round 3 measured as inherent to consecutive captures, or by the ticking numbers a fixture cannot pin. `head`/`refreshedAtHead` name the commit the frames were taken from, `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` the tip's trees the gate compares against, and the commits between them are the repair commit that kept `main`'s header and attachment work beside this branch's pane, the two fix commits, and this evidence commit — none of which is mounted differently by a captured story except the two the frames are FOR. `partialCapture.addedAtHead` names the commit the round-1 pass added these frames at, re-pointed here at the commit the branch's rebases replayed it as: `check-evidence.mjs` holds every head citation to `head`'s own bar, and that citation was the one field in this set's record that had gone stale (it resolved to a dangling object that only existed in this clone).
partialCapture.branchAddition: THIS PR added 27 run-panel surfaces and 54 frames as first drafted, six more surfaces and twelve frames in the review round, four more surfaces and eight frames in the design round, and two more surfaces and four frames in round 1's batched remediation (the roster's membership and the descend control) - 39 surfaces, 78 frames. The set is a NARROWED capture over a branch, not a sweep, so it does not move the swept total by itself; what moves the swept total is the tree, and `countsMean.frames` is where the current figure lives (882 frames outside every declared set, of 1054 committed at this head). Round 2 re-took all 78 of them - bytes, not counts: the set's own size is unchanged, and the re-take is recorded in the note below.

supplementary.capturedAtHeadNote: Re-driven at the head the branch stood on before an earlier rebase (`8fc94e602`, orphaned by that force-push), and cited as that commit's replay in this history, because the re-drive is what the citation has to rest on and a replay is the only spelling of it this history carries. The chain is `8fc94e602` -> `71cd00ae0` (the rebase onto 0.19.7) -> `72225e78f` (this rebase), each a replay of the one before it. The re-drive was exact: the app was RE-BUILT from that tree (`pnpm build` with `VITE_LOCAL_OPERATOR_API_URL` pointing at the scratch backend, which the run verifies the built renderer carries) and driven through the same isolated harness twice, and a fresh encode of each new PNG along the same lossy path (`magick -quality 88`, the setting the swept frames use) hashed to the committed git blob - `d6498ce493` (files-panel/dark), `b016a285d2` (pdf-viewer/light), `bbd1c35bec` (video-viewer/dark), `c2e8c5e987` (video-viewer/light) - so nothing was rewritten and the pixels on disk are that pass's own output, not an earlier pass's carried forward. Every reading the driver takes was unchanged: the same six mentioned paths in the same order with `march-export.csv` carrying `No longer on disk`, six tiles under the panel head, the PDF inside Chromium's viewer on a `blob:` URL titled `PDF: invoice-review.pdf` with the open-in-OS control and zero CSP violations, and the video `readyState 4 / currentTime 1.2 / duration 2 / 480x270 / error null` on the media route (the driver refuses to write a video frame unless the clip decodes). The crop was unchanged too: the panel's own measured rect, 1598x1932+1858+0 at a 1728x966 CSS viewport, dpr 2. Neither this rebase nor the one before it re-drove the set, and the reason is in `provenanceNote`: the frames are cropped to the canvas panel, so the sidebar this rebase's delta touches is not in them at all, and the frame-to-source question is settled by the byte-identical re-drive rather than by re-running it. One harness note for the next pass, recorded because the fix belongs to the gitignored harness rather than to this set: the driver's process is held alive by its spawned Electron child after it has written its report, so the runner stalls between the two theme passes; ending only that child (the PID the run started, never a process found by name) lets the pass continue.

supplementary.source: the REAL built Electron app (`pnpm build`, then `docs/evidence/window-mode/harness/run.sh` with EXTRA_SEED=seed-model-picker.mjs and DRIVE_SCRIPT=drive-model-picker.mjs, headless, 1380x900) against an isolated `local-operator serve` on a port the script owns, 0 frontmost samples in every run and 0 renderer errors. Sixteen states, and they come from TWO runs because two starting states are needed: fifteen from the branch's own seed (no provider credential, i.e. the refusal path — the seed the `before-*` halves were taken under, so the pairs still differ by the change and not by the setup), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames from a second run on QA's credentialed seed (`/tmp/qa130/seed-qa.mjs`, a synthetic `openai` credential written through the backend's own AuthStore) — without a credential the owner refuses every switch, so a switch it ACCEPTS does not exist there. The second run's frames are prefixed `cred-` by the driver so no frame can be mistaken for the other seed's. `localOperatorDark` is the app's own default theme, which is the only theme the harness boots into. **U7 round.** The one frame UX U7 invalidated was re-captured on the fixed head and one `before-*` half was added beside it: `needs-sign-in-pick-settled` now shows `This session runs anthropic/claude-opus-5.` (the row the check is on) where the pre-fix frame showed `openai/gpt-4.1`, and that pre-fix frame is committed as `before-header-names-the-switch` — the only `before-*` half taken on this branch's own pre-fix head (`ccbeb0e2a`) rather than on the merge-base, because UX filed U7 against the branch rather than against the base. That run is also the first whose cache lives inside the scratch root: `run.sh` now sets `HOME="$SCRATCH/home"` (QA round 2, Q3 — the catalogue cache resolves from `HOME`, not from the config dir), so the seed copies the same `*.listing.json` files the earlier run read into the scratch home, and nothing outside `/tmp` is written. Both runs' measurements are committed beside the frames (`picker-metrics.json`, `picker-metrics-credentialed.json`), so every number the README quotes is re-derivable from the tree.
supplementary.why: the claim is that a hover, a keyboard highlight, an in-flight pick and the OUTCOME of that pick are perceivable — properties of computed style and of timing that no palette assertion and no component test can see. The unit suite asserts the classes, the transitions and the reading rule (`scripts/picker-feedback.test.mjs`); only a frame of the running app shows the ground and the edge the row actually paints inside a dialog whose own ground is `elevated`, and what the user is left with when the answer arrives after the dialog is gone. The `before-*` halves carry the defect as a measurement: the active row's computed background is `rgb(40,35,24)`, identical to the dialog's, and `before-pointer-left-list` is byte-identical to `before-keyboard-highlight` (AE 0 of 4,813,440 px). Seven of the sixteen states are after-only, and that is the finding rather than an omission: each is a state the old code could not produce or could not report — the pointer's structural edge in a palette where the wash collapses (D12), the footer naming the row Enter acts on while that row is off screen (U1), the band holding a labelled spinner while the pick is unconfirmed (U3), the refusal landing with the dialog already closed (U2), and the three `needs-sign-in-*` frames (Q1). The transcript note count is measured either side of the U2 case — 1 before the click, 2 after it, with the dialog closed 80 ms in — because the refusal sentence is identical for every refused pick and only a count can prove a second one was written. The U7 pair is measured rather than described: between the two frames AE is 85,307 px (1.77%) of 4,813,440, of which 13,230 px (2% fuzz) sit in one 952x64 band across the header sentence's own text line and 274 px are the clock.
